The management plugin for the Panellist in the DSH (DeepSeek Harness) client.

The Panellist is the column on the left of the session UI: the global entries contributed by individual plugins — plugins, automation tasks, skill center, memory system, SSH, MCP connectors… They come from different plugins, each declares its own order, and each decides its own icon and name.

dsh-panellist README · dsh-panellist：This plugin lets the **user** take over: which Panel entries appear on the rail, in what order they appear, what they are called, what icon they use, and which entries are folded into a Group. All configuration is done in a new tab in Settings, and changes take effect immediately.

dsh-panellist README · dsh-panellist：> Status: **implemented**. This README pair is the whole specification — there is no separate design document: behaviour is §2–§3, the configuration and the interfaces are §4, the compatibility contract is §5, how to install it is §6, and how it is built is §7. The normative configuration shape is [`docs/schema/config.schema.json`](docs/schema/config.schema.json).
>
> Three refinements to the original design (all discovered during implementation and backfilled into this document): the rail id of a Group is `dsh-panellist:<groupId>`; unconfigured Panel entries are always listed on the rail, but an `order` is written only once the Sequence is non-empty (i.e. after your first structural change); and the `/panellist/api/reveal` endpoint was added to implement "Open config file".

dsh-panellist README · 1. Why it is needed：The DSH Panellist is a **read-only projection**: the shell enumerates the registrations in the `sidebar.panellist` slot and renders them sorted by the order **each item reported at registration time**. No official API is provided for rewriting someone else's registration:

dsh-panellist README · 1. Why it is needed：1. **Registry rewrite** — rewrite the order, name and icon component on the registration at runtime (the registration object is not frozen and is handed back by the slot registry, so a post-hoc write is visible to the shell); this plugin's changes do not touch any plugin's own page.
2. **Minimal DOM/CSS reprojection** — only one thing cannot be done through the registry: taking a row off the rail. Group rows are registrations too (registered by this plugin), so their row box, highlight, tooltip and collapsed-state behavior still come from the shell; the popup menu is an overlay and does not modify native rows.

dsh-panellist README · 2.1 What it manages：- **All** registrations in the Panellist are treated alike: kernel-shipped items (plugins, automation tasks, skill center, memory system, SSH, MCP connectors) and items registered by third-party plugins can all be managed.
- This plugin's own settings tab is not in the Panellist, so it is not managed.
- Real Panel entry ids are discovered at runtime and are not hard-coded; the ids in this document's examples are illustrative only.
- The rail's own **More** row is listed as well, although the shell — not a Panellist contributor — renders it (§2.12).
dsh-panellist README · 2.2 Sequence model：The Sequence is a series of **ordered items**, each of which is either a **single Panel entry** or a **Group**:

dsh-panellist README · 2.2 Sequence model：The design conversation settled the notation this way (`G{…}` = one Group):

| Notation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `a c b d e` | `[a][c][b][d][e]` |
| `a b c` | `[a][b][c]` |
| `a dropdown(b c d e)` | `[a][G{b,c,d,e}]` |
| `a dropdown(b d e c)` | `[a][G{b,d,e,c}]` |
| `a dropdown(b e c)d` | `[a][G{b,e,c}][d]` |
| `dropdown(a b c)d e` | `[G{a,b,c}][d][e]` |

dsh-panellist README · 2.3 Shown / Hidden：- There are only two states: **Shown** / **Hidden** (there is no third "disabled" state).
- Hidden = it no longer appears on the rail, but the Panel entry itself still exists and is still usable (it can be selected from the management panel, and activated by other plugins or keyboard shortcuts), and the functionality of the plugin it belongs to is unaffected.
- Exception: **if a Hidden Panel entry is currently active, its row is shown temporarily** — avoiding the case where "the user is still on this page, but the rail has no entry for it".
- **Members of a Group can be hidden too**, where "hidden" means "left out of the Group menu": a member's rail row is already suppressed by the Group, so for a member hiding only affects the flyout. The member stays in the Group — the count, the ordering and the Group trigger highlight all still see it.
- **A missing member is left out of the Group menu automatically** (its registration is gone, and a disabled "missing" row in the menu only took up room the user cannot act on). It stays in the configuration and in the settings page's "missing panels" list, waiting to be cleaned up.

dsh-panellist README · 2.4 Label override：- A pure display-layer override, affecting only three places: the text of the rail row, the tooltip text in the collapsed state, and the accessible name.
- It does not change same-name displays elsewhere in DSH (Settings, command palette, etc.), and does not change the original name declared by the contributor.
- The first version is a **single string**, effective for all languages.
dsh-panellist README · 2.5 Icon override：The **settings navigation row has its own dedicated glyph** (a panel list, at the heavier `Icon*OutlineMedium` 1.3px weight that column is drawn at) — see §3.

dsh-panellist README · 2.6 Groups and Group triggers：- A Group trigger has its **own** icon and name; by default they are pre-filled from the icon and name of the "first item in the Group" (a common name is "More"), and the user can change them. When no name is set, the trigger text is resolved from the first live member at render time — nothing is baked into the config.
- The Group trigger's **whole row is clickable**, and clicking it expands the Group menu; a whole-row click is always used to expand the menu and never navigates to a page. The menu lists the Group's members and nothing else: an "Overview" link to the Group's own page used to sit in its title row and was removed on user feedback. That page still exists as the Group's `main` fallback (so selecting the Group id programmatically cannot error) but has no entry point of its own.
- When any item in the Group is active, the **Group trigger is highlighted**, so the user can tell which Group the current page is in without expanding the menu.
- When a Group is created, it is inserted at **the original position of its topmost member** — that is, the Group "grows" where its members already were. The model guarantees this (`cre

dsh-panellist README · 2.7 Group menu：- **Opens on click** (not on hover, to avoid accidental activation).
- Lists the members the user can act on: a member that is hidden (§2.3) or missing is left out, and a Group whose members are all hidden says so instead of showing an empty card.
- Keyboard accessible: `Enter`/`Space` expands, `Esc` closes, and the up/down arrow keys move within the Group.
- When the sidebar is collapsed into the 56 px rail, the menu always **flies out to the right** (flyout).
- The menu scrolls when the number of items in the Group exceeds the visible height; the first version does **not** do an in-Group search box.

dsh-panellist README · 2.8 Unconfigured items and Orphans：- A newly installed plugin registers a Panel entry you have not touched yet → it is **listed in the sequence straight away** (after the configured entries, arranged by its own order); there is nothing to opt into first.
- The contributor of a Panel entry is uninstalled while the config still holds it → the config is **kept**, the management panel marks it "missing", and offers a "Clean up orphans" button.
- Until you make a STRUCTURAL change (a drag, creating or dissolving a group), this plugin writes **no order at all**: the rail keeps the order its contributors chose. A rename, a re-icon or a hide only overrides that one entry and leaves the order alone — which is what "we do not touch what you did not ask us to touch" means in practice.

dsh-panellist README · 2.9 How a change takes effect：Config changes **take effect immediately**: no need to restart DSH, no need to reload any plugin, and no need to reload the page. That holds for *every* edit, including the ones that write nothing at all: the rewrite pass compares a digest of everything the rail renders (order, name, icon, shown/hidden) and re-projects when it moves, so a second icon pick or a second rename lands on the rail just like the first one did.

dsh-panellist README · 2.10 Scope of takeover：The management panel **lists the whole rail from the first time it is opened**: there is nothing to "adopt" before you can touch a Panel entry, and there is no "not taken over yet" list. (An earlier design had a "not configured" list with per-item take-over / release buttons; it was removed on user feedback — it only added a step. A banner plus a "use the current rail order as a starting point" button went the same way: the list is the rail either way, so the gate is invisible.)
dsh-panellist README · 2.10 Scope of takeover：What still holds is the **minimal-intervention property in what gets WRITTEN**, not in the UI:

dsh-panellist README · 2.10 Scope of takeover：- The config's `sequence` is **partially authoritative**: it records only what you actually changed.
- A `sequence` that is empty means **no `order` is written at all** (the state right after installation, a pure no-op), and an unconfigured Panel's name/icon/hidden state is left entirely alone; it keeps the contributor's own order.
- Your first structural change (a drag, a merge into a Group) writes the current order out as an explicit sequence; unconfigured entries stay after the configured block in their own native order (§2.8).

dsh-panellist README · 2.10 Scope of takeover：Implementation (`src/shared/model.ts`): `rows` is always the whole rail (an unconfigured row's `order` is `null`, meaning "do not write"), while `reordering` decides whether an `order` is written at all.

dsh-panellist README · 2.11 One live mount per page：The shell may apply a client bundle more than once on one page (it re-evaluates a bundle whose file changed, an HMR pass re-applies it). Two controllers over one ledger fight: the second one captures the first one's glyph wrappers as if the contributors had installed them, and both write the same entries. `apply` therefore retires the previous mount before building its own (`src/client/mount.ts`), and every wrapper this plugin installs is recognisable, so an entry still holding one is unwrapped rather than adopted (§7.2).

dsh-panellist README · 2.12 The shell's own "More" row：The rail's last row, **More**, is not a Panellist registration: DSH renders it itself, from the `sidebar.panellist.actions` slot, and portals the menu it opens to `document.body`. So it is not a `sidebar.panellist` entry — no `order`, no label thunk, no glyph component for this plugin to rewrite (§7.2). It is listed in the sequence all the same, because it is an ordinary flex child of the same `nav`:

dsh-panellist README · 2.12 The shell's own "More" row：- **Position.** The row (`shell:more`) takes a place in the sequence like any other and can be dragged or moved up and down. The rewrite pass writes the rail in DOM order, so its index says exactly how many rows precede it; the injected rule gives the More anchor `order: 1` and every row from that position on `order: 2`, which parks it exactly there with flexbox. No other row selector is touched, and while the row is already last nothing is written at all.
- **Hide.** Hiding it takes the entry point to the panel menu with it, so hide it only if you do not use that menu.

dsh-panellist README · 2.12 The shell's own "More" row：By design it cannot be renamed, re-iconed or grouped: its name, glyph and behaviour belong to the shell, and it has no page to open, so it can neither start a group nor be folded into one — its appearance editor says exactly that instead of offering the controls. One caveat: what moves is its **painted** position; **keyboard order does not** follow, so Tab still reaches it last, where the DOM puts it. (Every other row is different: their order is written into the registration itself, so the shell renders them in the new order and their tab order follows.)

dsh-panellist README · 2.12 The shell's own "More" row：**Older shells are handled by measurement, not by a version check.** Probe 5 (§5) reports what the rail actually contains, and only two of its answers mean "there is no row": a panel list holding nothing but rows, and a list whose non-row child no longer matches. In both cases the row is left out of the sequence, so an unsupported build shows no dead entry. If the profile already configures it — a stored position, or a saved Hide — the row stays listed and carries a `Not painted here` badge instead, because dropping it would hand that setting to orphan cleanup. A rail that is merely not mounted (collapsed sidebar) is *unknown*, not absent, and unknown keeps the row.
dsh-panellist README · 3. Settings tab：Page content:

dsh-panellist README · 3.1 Sequence editor：- Lists the whole rail — every Panel entry from the first open, with nothing to adopt first.
- **Drag and drop** is the main channel: reorder, drag a row into an existing Group, drag a member back out.
- Each row's **"Group with next"** creates a Group; a Group row's **"Ungroup"** dissolves one.
- **Move up / Move down** are the keyboard fallback.
- Every row carries a **"Hide"/"Show"** button that toggles that row in place — Group rows included, and the **member rows inside a Group** too (a hidden member leaves the Group menu, §2.3).
- Clicking a row's name opens that row's appearance editor (§3.2), including a Group's members, which have no row of their own.
- The shell's own **More** row is in the list too, tagged `Shell row`; only its position and its visibility are editable there (§2.12).

dsh-panellist README · 3.2 Appearance override for an item：- **Name**: a single string override (§2.4).
- **Icon**: keep the original / the built-in set / paste SVG (§2.5), with a live preview. Picking a built-in icon previews it at the row's own size, and the preview for "keep the original" shows the contributor's real component.
- Visibility is the per-row **"Hide"/"Show"** button in the sequence list — one entry point, not two.
- A panel shown inside a Group says so here, so it is obvious why its rail row is not on the rail.

dsh-panellist README · 3.3 Group editing：- The Group trigger's name and icon.
- The ordered member list: move a member up/down, take it out of the Group, hide or show it.

dsh-panellist README · 3.4 Config import / export：Import validates the document before writing it; export serialises the whole file (all profiles). A failed import reports the field-level reason and changes nothing.
dsh-panellist README · 3.5 Open config file：`POST /panellist/api/reveal` opens `$DSH_HOME/panellist.json` in the system file manager. The path is also printed next to the button.

dsh-panellist README · 3.6 Missing panels：Configured ids with no registration are collected here with a count, and **"Clean up missing panels"** removes them — after an explicit confirmation, never automatically.

dsh-panellist README · 3.7 Self-check status：The result of the four startup probes (§5) with a **"Re-run self-check"** button. A failed probe shows what it measured, what is therefore disabled, and the DSH version the plugin measured.

This plugin depends on five **internal** facts about DSH (none of them a public contract), so it self-checks each one at startup:

dsh-panellist README · 5. Compatibility, self-checks, and degradation：| Internal fact relied on | Consequence when it breaks | How it is probed (`src/client/rail/probe.ts`) | Degradation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The slot registration object is not frozen, so `order`/`label`/icon component can be rewritten afterwards | Order, name, and icon cannot be changed | Temporarily register a probe row, rewrite its `order`, and read it back through `entriesOfSlot`; also check that neither the object nor its `options` is frozen | Disable rewriting, read-only |

Compatibility, self-checks, and degradation：- **The probes wait for the rail slot to exist before measuring.** `sidebar.panellist` is declared by the sidebar entry's children table and this plugin can mount before it; registering a probe row then is refused, and that one refusal is what read-only keys off. The run waits on the shell's own "run this when the seat exists" seam (`slots.inject`) first, bounded at 5 s, so a boot-order race can never park the plugin in read-only. A shell that never declares the slot is reported honestly after the wait.
- If any self-check fails → **degrade to read-only**: no further rewriting is done, the top of the management panel gives a clear notice (which item failed, what it affects, and how to report it), and the "Re-run self-check" button is kept.

CI checks the tag against `package.json` and calls `npm publish` (`lib/` is not committed, so that step is also what produces the published files).

dsh-panellist README · 7.2 The rewrite pass and the nudge：- **Compare before write, always.** Every writer compares first and every generated value (the label thunk, the glyph wrapper) is cached per captured registration. That is not a style preference: a fresh identity on every pass would never compare equal, so the pass would report a change, nudge, and re-enter itself forever. The controller additionally bounds a burst at `CASCADE_LIMIT` passes and logs a warning.
- **A nudge is owed by the plan, not by the write.** A raw field write bumps no ledger version, so nothing re-renders. After a batch of writes the pass registers a throwaway row and disposes it in the same task, which mutates the ledger twice and makes the shell re-read `order`/`label`. An edit that changes only what our own wrapper paints (a second built-in icon on a panel that already has one, a rename resolved by the already-installed thunk) writes no field at all — so the pass also compares a **digest of everything the rail renders** (order, label, icon, hidden, suppressed; panels and groups) and nudges when it moves, even with nothing to write. text: dsh-panellist README · 7.3 The DOM footprint：One stylesheet, injected once and adopted by a document id so a re-evaluated bundle cannot produce a second copy. Hiding is a single `:has()` rule over `nav[class*="_panelList"] > button[class*="_panelRow"]` — a row whose glyph rendered a marker span disappears. Because the marker is rendered by React, the rule is declarative: no observer, no re-parenting, no layout thrash. `hidden` = "hide unless this row is the active panel"; `suppressed` = "always hide, it is shown inside a Group instead". A second, equally declarative rule places the shell's own More row (§2.12): the anchor takes `order: 1` and the rows that must follow it `order: 2`, so the flex container paints it at the sequence position the user chose without moving a single node; the rule is only emitted while there is something to move.

dsh-panellist README · 7.4 Group rows and their menu：A Group row is a **genuine registration** of ours into `sidebar.panellist`, with its own `main` page under the same key: the shell places it by `order`, renders its `label`, and reuses both as the accessible name and the collapsed tooltip. `sync()` is idempotent — it re-registers only rows whose order or resolved label actually changed, because a needless re-registration would remount a row the user may be interacting with.

dsh-panellist README · 7.4 Group rows and their menu：The row is a single `<button>` owned by the shell, so the trigger glyph installs **capture-phase** `click`/`keydown` listeners on its ancestor button: capture runs before React's delegated handler at the root, so one `stopPropagation()` keeps the shell's own `selectPanel` from ever running, and `preventDefault()` cancels the row's default activation. The menu itself is a body-portal overlay positioned from the row's `getBoundingClientRect()`, so it can escape the sidebar's overflow; it is measured before being shown, and it closes on `Esc` or an outside click.

dsh-panellist README · 7.4 Group rows and their menu：The Group highlight comes from the layout's own public reader (`ctx.layout.panelInfo`), not from the shell's `aria-current`: the shell highlights a row only when the row *is* the active panel, and a Group row never is, so membership drives the highlight instead.

dsh-panellist README · 7.5 The settings navigation marker：The `settings.section` contract has no icon field and the shell picks the nav glyph from a closed list by section id, so the row is located by its **visible text**: a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` matches `[role="dialog"] nav button` against our own localized label and stamps `data-dsh-panellist-settings-nav`, and the stylesheet hides the shell's own `<svg>` in that row and paints our masked glyph in front of it. All of it is removed on dispose, and if nothing matches, the native gear stays and the failure is reported through the self-check — never an error.

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）客户端「面板列表」的管理插件。

面板列表（panellist）是会话界面左侧那一列由各个插件贡献的全局入口——插件、自动化任务、技能中心、记忆系统、SSH、MCP 连接器……它们来自不同的插件，顺序由各自声明，图标与名称也由各自决定。

本插件让**用户**接管这件事：哪些页签出现在轨道上、以什么顺序出现、叫什么名字、用什么图标，以及把若干页签收进一个分组。所有配置都在「设置」里的一项新页签内完成，改动即时生效。

dsh-panellist README · 1. 为什么需要它：DSH 的面板列表是**只读投影**：外壳枚举 `sidebar.panellist` 槽位里的注册项，按每一项**注册时自报的**顺序排序渲染。官方没有提供任何改写他人注册的 API：

- 顺序只读——插件只能决定自己那一项的 `order`；
- 没有「分组」概念——一行就是一个页签；
- 图标由贡献者提供的组件决定，名称由贡献者的 `label` 决定；
- 「设置」导航页签的图标只能从内核内置的一份清单里挑。

因此本插件必须同时用两个杠杆，并且把 DOM 介入压到最小：

1. **注册表改写**——在运行时改写注册项上的顺序、名称与图标组件（注册项对象未被冻结，且由槽位注册表原样交回，所以事后写入对下一次投影可见）；本插件的改动不触碰任何插件的页面本身。
2. **最小 DOM/CSS 重投影**——只有一件事无法靠注册表完成：把某一行从轨道上「拿掉」。分组行本身也是注册项（由本插件注册），因此它的行框、高亮、提示与收起态行为依旧由外壳负责；弹出菜单是覆盖层，不改动原生行。

dsh-panellist README · 2.1 管理对象：- 面板列表里的**所有**注册项一视同仁：内核自带项（插件、自动化任务、技能中心、记忆系统、SSH、MCP 连接器）与第三方插件注册的项都可被管理。
- 本插件自己的设置页签不在面板列表内，因此不参与管理。
- 真实页签 id 在运行时发现，不硬编码；本文档示例里的 id 仅是示意。
- 轨道自带的**「更多」行**也会列出，虽然它由外壳渲染、并非 Panellist 贡献者（§2.12）。

dsh-panellist README · 2.2 序列模型：轨道序列是一串**有序项**，每一项要么是**单个页签**，要么是一个**分组**：

- 每个页签在整条序列中**恰好出现一次**（序列是对页签集合的划分，不重复）；
- 分组自身占据序列里的一个位置，并含有一个**有序的**页签子集；
- **只允许一层**嵌套（分组内不能再放分组）；
- 空分组非法；只含 1 项的允许，但管理面板会提示。

设计讨论里确认过的写法按此模型解释如下（`G{…}` = 一个分组）：

| 写法 | 解释 |
| --- | --- |
| `a c b d e` | `[a][c][b][d][e]` |
| `a b c` | `[a][b][c]` |
| `a 下拉（b c d e）` | `[a][G{b,c,d,e}]` |
| `a 下拉（b d e c）` | `[a][G{b,d,e,c}]` |
| `a 下拉（b e c）d` | `[a][G{b,e,c}][d]` |
| `下拉（a b c）d e` | `[G{a,b,c}][d][e]` |

dsh-panellist README · 2.3 显示 / 隐藏：- 只有两态：**显示** / **隐藏**（没有「禁用」第三态）。
- 隐藏 = 不再出现在轨道上，但页签本身依然存在、依然可用（可从管理面板选中、可被其它插件或快捷键激活），它所属插件的功能不受影响。
- 例外：**被隐藏的页签若正处于激活态，它那一行临时显示**——避免出现「人还在这个页面，轨道上却没有入口」。
- **分组内的成员也支持隐藏**，含义换成「不出现在分组菜单里」：成员的轨道行本来就被分组抑制掉了，所以对成员而言隐藏只作用于下拉菜单。成员仍留在组内——计数、排序、组头高亮都照旧看见它。
- **已缺失的成员自动不出现在分组菜单里**（注册项没了，菜单里留一行禁用的「已缺失」只是占地方，用户也无从操作）；它仍留在配置里、仍列在设置页的「已缺失的面板」里，等你清理。

dsh-panellist README · 2.4 名称覆盖：- 纯显示层覆盖，只影响三处：轨道行的文字、收起状态的提示文字、无障碍名称。
- 不改动 DSH 其它位置（设置、命令面板等）中的同名显示，也不改变贡献者声明的原始名称。
- 首版为**单字符串**，对所有语言生效。

dsh-panellist README · 2.5 图标覆盖：1. **保留原图标**（默认）； 2. **内置图标集**——本插件自带的 24 个内联矢量图形（零依赖，离线可用）。它们按**轨道上邻居们所用的规范**绘制，即 `Icon*OutlineRegular` 那一档：`viewBox="0 0 16 16"`、`fill="none"`、`stroke="currentColor"`、线宽 **1px**、几何落在 16 网格的半像素坐标上并大致收在 2…14 之内、圆头圆角、`aria-hidden`、无 id 与外部引用。其中三个直接采用外壳自己那几颗默认图标的美术数据，因此选上去和它要替代的项看起来完全一样：`puzzle` 是插件风车（`IconPluginPinwheelOutline`）、`clock` 是时钟（`IconClockOutline`）、`more` 是省略号（`IconEllipsisOutline`）。这套图形在 16px 下与上述官方美术并排比对，并逐个量过着墨包围盒； 3. **用户上传图标**——粘贴 SVG 源码； - 白名单净化：移除 `script`、`foreignObject`、事件属性、外部引用（`href`/`xlink:href` 指向外部的用例）； - 单个 SVG 上限 **64 KB**； - 内联渲染（不是 ``），因此能随主题变色。
dsh-panellist README · 2.5 图标覆盖：**设置导航那一行有它自己专用的图形**（一个「面板列表」，线宽取那一列所用的 `Icon*OutlineMedium` 1.3）——见 §3。

dsh-panellist README · 2.6 分组与组头：- 组头有**独立**的图标与名称，默认预填「组内第一项」的图标与名称（常用名如「更多」），用户可改。没设名称时，组头文字在渲染时按「第一个活着的成员」解析——配置里不烘焙字面量。
- 组头**整行可点**，点击即展开分组菜单；整行点击一律用于展开菜单，不会跳转页面。菜单里只列该分组的成员：标题行里原本还有一个指向分组自己那一页的「概览」入口，已按用户反馈删除。那一页仍保留为分组 `main` 的兜底页（这样程序化选中分组 id 时不会报错），但不再有任何自己的入口。
- 组内任一项处于激活态时，**组头高亮**，用户不展开菜单也能看出当前页面在哪个组里。
- 拖拽新建分组时，分组插到**「最靠上的那个成员」原来的位置**，即分组「长在」它成员的原地。这条规则由模型保证（`createGroup` 以「最靠上成员上方那一行」的身份为锚点），因此与具体手势无关。

dsh-panellist README · 2.7 分组菜单：- **点击展开**（悬停不展开，避免误触）。
- 只列用户能操作的成员：隐藏的（§2.3）与已缺失的都不出现；组内成员全部隐藏时，菜单写明这一点，而不是给一张空卡片。
- 键盘可达：`Enter`/`Space` 展开、`Esc` 关闭、上下方向键在组内移动。
- 侧栏收起成 56 px 轨道时，菜单一律**向右弹出**（flyout）。
- 组内项数超过可视高度时菜单可滚动；首版**不做**组内搜索框。

dsh-panellist README · 2.8 未配置项与孤儿：- 新装的插件注册了一个你还没动过的页签 → 它**直接出现在序列里**（在已配置项之后，按它自身的顺序），不需要先「纳入」它。
- 某个页签的贡献者被卸载、而配置里还留着它 → 配置**保留**，管理面板标注「已缺失」，并提供「清理孤儿」按钮。
- 在你**做结构性改动之前**（拖动、建组/解散分组），本插件**不写任何顺序**：轨道保持贡献者自己的顺序。改名、换图标、隐藏只覆盖那一项、不动顺序——这正是「不碰你没让我碰的东西」的落点。
dsh-panellist README · 2.9 生效方式：配置改动**即时生效**：不需要重启 DSH，不需要重载任何插件，也不需要重新加载页面。这对**每一次**改动都成立，包括那些「什么都不用写」的改动：改写环节会比较一份「轨道渲染所依赖的一切」（顺序、名称、图标、显示/隐藏）的摘要，只要它变了就重新投影——所以第二次换图标、第二次改名，和第一次一样立刻上轨道。

dsh-panellist README · 2.10 接管范围：管理面板里**从第一次打开起就列出整条轨道**：不需要先把某个页签「纳入」才能碰它，也不存在一份「还没接管」的清单。（中途曾有过「未配置清单 + 逐项接管 / 恢复原生」的设计，已按用户反馈删除——它们只是让人多点一步；后来那条「还没接管顺序」的说明横幅与「以当前轨道顺序作为起点」按钮也一并删掉了：列表本身就是轨道，这道门槛不可见。）

真正仍然成立的「最小干预」性质落在**写入**上，而不是界面上：

- 配置里的 `sequence` 是**部分权威**：只记你实际改过的东西。
- `sequence` 为空时**不写任何 `order`**（新装即如此，纯 no-op），未配置项的名字/图标/隐藏一概不碰；它们保持贡献者自己的顺序。
- 你第一次做结构性改动（拖动、合并分组）时，当前顺序会被写成显式序列；此后未配置项仍按各自的原生顺序列在已配置块之后（§2.8）。

实现见 `src/shared/model.ts`：`rows` 永远是整条轨道（未配置的行 `order` 为 `null`，即「不改」），而 `reordering` 决定是否真的写 `order`。

dsh-panellist README · 2.11 每页只允许一个挂载：外壳可能在同一页里把客户端 bundle 应用两次（文件变了会重新求值，HMR 也会再应用一次）。两个控制器同时操作同一份账本会互相打架：后来者会把前一个装上去的图标包装当成贡献者自己的组件，双方还都往同一批注册项上写。因此 `apply` 在构建自己的挂载之前先退役上一个（`src/client/mount.ts`），并且本插件装上去的每个包装都是**可识别**的——遇到还挂着包装的注册项会先拆开再接管（§7.2）。

dsh-panellist README · 2.12 外壳自带的「更多」行：轨道最后一行**「更多」**不是 Panellist 的注册项：它由 DSH 自己渲染（来自 `sidebar.panellist.actions` 槽位），点开的侧边菜单被 portal 到 `document.body`。所以它不是 `sidebar.panellist` 的条目——没有 `order`、没有名称 thunk、没有图标组件可以让本插件改写（§7.2）。但它同样是那个 `nav` 里的普通 flex 子节点，因此仍然出现在序列里：

- **位置。** 该行（`shell:more`）在序列里占一个位置，可以拖拽或上移/下移。改写环节按 DOM 顺序写轨道，所以它在序列里的下标就说明了它前面有多少行；注入的规则给「更多」锚点 `order: 1`、给它所在位置及其后的每一行 `order: 2`，用 flex 把它精确停在那里。不改动任何其他行选择器；当它本来就在最后时，一条规则也不写。
- **隐藏。** 隐藏它就等于去掉面板菜单的入口，所以只在你不用那个菜单时才隐藏。

dsh-panellist README · 2.12 外壳自带的「更多」行：按设计它不能被改名、换图标或并入分组：名称、图标与行为都属于外壳，而且它没有可打开的页面，既不能作为分组的开头，也不能被折进分组——它的外观编辑会直接说明这一点，而不是给出那些控件。还有一个注意点：移动的是它**画出来的位置**，**键盘顺序并不跟随**，Tab 仍按 DOM 位置最后到达它。（其他行不同：它们的顺序写进注册对象本身，外壳按新顺序渲染，键盘顺序也随之改变。）

**旧版本靠探测处理，不比较版本号。** 探测 5（§5）如实报告轨道里到底有什么，只有两种结果表示「没有这一行」：面板列表里除了行以外什么都没有，以及列表里那个非行的子节点不再匹配。这两种情况下该行不出现在序列里，于是不支持的版本上不会留下一条死条目。如果这个配置里已经写过它——存过位置，或点过隐藏——该行仍会列出，并带一个「当前版本无此行」标记，因为直接丢掉等于把它交给孤儿清理。仅仅「轨道没挂载」（侧边栏收起）属于*未知*而不是「没有」，未知时保留该行。

dsh-panellist README · 3. 设置页签：在「设置」对话框左侧新增一项：

- 名称：**面板列表**；位置：排在设置导航靠后；
- 图标：**自己专用的图形**——一个「面板列表」，线宽取那一列统一的 `Icon*OutlineMedium`（1.3），以 `currentColor` 蒙版画在外壳原本的兜底齿轮位置。设置导航的契约里没有图标字段，所以这一行按可见文本定位并打标记；探测失败则保留原生齿轮（不报错）。见 §7.5。
- 页面**没有「完成」按钮**：关窗由对话框自己的 X 负责。

dsh-panellist README · 3.1 序列编辑器：- 列出整条轨道（从一开始就是全部页签，无需先「纳入」）。
- 主通道是**拖拽**：排序、拖入已有分组、把成员拖出分组。
- 每行的**「与下一项合并为分组」**建组；分组行的**「解散分组」**拆组。
- 键盘兜底是每项的**上移/下移**。
- 每行还有**「隐藏」/「显示」**按钮，就地切换这一行的可见性——分组行、以及**分组内的成员行**同样适用（成员隐藏后不再出现在分组菜单里，见 §2.3）。按钮排在每行最后（`↑ ↓ − 隐藏`），和顶层行一致。

dsh-panellist README · 5. 兼容性、自检与降级：**版本门槛**：`engines.dsh: ">=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0"`（与开发所用的内核版本一致；类型包在 npm 上同版本可取，因此编译期就能发现契约漂移）。

本插件依赖 DSH 的五条**内部**事实（都不是公开契约），因此启动时逐项自检：

dsh-panellist README · 5. 兼容性、自检与降级：| 依赖的内部事实 | 失效后的后果 | 探测方式（`src/client/rail/probe.ts`） | 降级 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 槽位注册项对象未被冻结，可事后改写 `order`/`label`/图标组件 | 顺序、名称、图标改不动 | 临时注册一个探针行，改写它的 `order` 再通过 `entriesOfSlot` 回读；同时检查对象与 `options` 都未被冻结 | 停用改写，只读 |
| 轨道行的 DOM 结构可被定位，且 CSS 支持 `:has()` 选择器 | 「隐藏」这一项无法生效 | `CSS.supports('selector(:has(*))')`，并用**与隐藏规则完全相同**的选择器数行数，与 rail 注册项数比对（轨道未挂载时记为通过并写明原因） | 停用隐藏（其余改写保留），只读提示 |
| 外壳仍把「是否激活」传给图标组件（隐藏中的激活页签需要它） | 隐藏中的激活页签无法临时显示 | 临时注册一个探针行，等两帧确认它的图标组件确实被渲染、且收到的 `active` 是布尔值 | 该规则失效：隐藏变为无条件隐藏 |
| 设置导航按钮可由可见文本定位 | 设置页签图标换不了 | 对话框打开时按文本匹配自己的行；未打开时记为通过并写明（标记由 `MutationObserver` 在每次打开时重跑） | 保留原生齿轮图标 |
| 外壳把自带的「更多」行渲染为轨道列表最后一个非按钮子节点，其类名带 `_moreAnchor` | 「更多」行保持原生位置，无法移动或隐藏 | 用 `nav[class*="_panelList"] > span[class*="_moreAnchor"]` 匹配；轨道未挂载，或根本没有「更多」行（`sidebar.panellist.actions` 无人注册）时记为通过并写明是哪种情况；其他非按钮子节点会被报出类名。两种「没有这一行」的结论也正是把该行从序列中去掉的依据——除非配置里已经写过它（§2.12） | 只有这一行失去位置与隐藏能力；在没有该行的版本上，未配置过的行根本不会列出 |

dsh-panellist README · 5. 兼容性、自检与降级：- **探针会先等轨道槽位存在再测。** `sidebar.panellist` 由侧边栏条目的 `children` 表声明，而本插件可能比它先挂载；此时注册探针行会被拒，而「只读」正是由这一次拒绝触发的。所以这一轮会先等外壳自己的「席位出现后再跑」这条缝（`slots.inject`），上限 5 秒——启动顺序的竞态不会再让插件卡在只读。始终不声明该槽位的外壳，会在超时后如实报出。
- 任一项自检失败 → **降级为只读**：不再做任何改写，管理面板顶部给出明确提示（哪一项失败、影响什么、如何反馈），并保留「重新自检」按钮。
- 绝不静默半坏，也不阻止插件加载（DSH 升级后界面仍然可用）。
- 已知不确定性：DSH 的样式类名是**构建哈希**，会在发版时重掷。因此选择器一律使用「稳定后缀」匹配（例如 `[class*="_panelRow"]`，实测有效；`[class$="_panelRow"]` 在激活行上会失败），并且每次挂载都重新探测一次。

dsh-panellist README · 7.1 模块布局：```
dsh-panellist/
├─ src/
│  ├─ index.ts                # 宿主半入口（重新导出 plugin/index）
│  ├─ plugin/                 # 宿主半：配置存储、本机路由、迁移与损坏回退
dsh-panellist README · 7.2 改写环节与同步抖动：`registry/rail.tsx` 读取轨道槽位，第一次见到某个注册项时记下它原本的 `order`/`label`/组件，此后只写有差异的部分。三条后果值得知道：

dsh-panellist README · 7.2 改写环节与同步抖动：- **写前必比。** 每个写入者都先比较，每个生成值（label thunk、图标包装）都按注册项缓存。这不是风格偏好：每次都是新身份就永远比不相等，于是这一轮报告「有变化」→ 抖动 → 再次进入，永不收敛。控制器另外把一次连发限制在 `CASCADE_LIMIT` 轮，并打日志告警。
- **该不该抖动由计划决定，而不是由写入决定。** 字段直写不增加账本版本，所以没有任何重渲染。写完一批之后，这一轮会注册一个一次性行并在同一任务里销毁它——账本因此变更两次，外壳就会重读 `order`/`label`。而只改变「我们自己的包装所绘制的东西」的编辑（给已经带内置图标的面板再选一个内置图标、被已装好的 thunk 解析的第二次改名）一个字段都不写——所以这一轮**同时**比较一份「轨道渲染所依赖的一切」摘要（顺序、名称、图标、隐藏、抑制；面板与分组），只要它动了就抖动，哪怕无字段可写。挂载的第一轮只记住摘要、绝不因此抖动，所以新装仍是严格 no-op。
- **我们的包装是可识别的。** 包装在行被隐藏时渲染标记而非图形，而贡献者的组件只存在于它的闭包里——任何回读 `entry.component` 的地方都可能拿到我们自己的包装。因此每个包装都登记进一个页面级 `WeakMap`（包装 → 取被捕获组件的 getter）；捕获环节发现是自己的包装就先拆开并认领该槽位，`nativeGlyph` 出口再拆一次。没有这一步时，隐藏面板与分组成员在设置页里的预览是一个空盒子。

dsh-panellist README · 7.3 DOM 足迹：只有一张样式表，注入一次并按 document id 复用（bundle 被重新求值也不会出现第二份）。隐藏是一条 `:has()` 规则，作用在 `nav[class*="_panelList"] > button[class*="_panelRow"]` 上——glyph 里渲染出标记 span 的行会消失。因为标记由 React 渲染，这条规则是声明式的：没有观察器、没有挪动节点、没有布局抖动。`hidden` = 「除非自己是激活页否则隐藏」；`suppressed` = 「无条件隐藏，它显示在分组里」。还有一条同样声明式的规则负责摆放外壳自带的「更多」行（§2.12）：锚点取 `order: 1`，必须排在它后面的行取 `order: 2`，于是 flex 容器把它画在用户选定的序列位置上，一个节点都不挪；而且只有确实需要移动时才会输出这条规则。

dsh-panellist README · 7.4 分组行与分组菜单：分组行是本插件向 `sidebar.panellist` 的**真实注册**，并在同一个 key 上带一个 `main` 页：外壳按 `order` 摆放它、渲染它的 `label`，并把两者同时用作无障碍名称与收起态提示。`sync()` 是幂等的——只有顺序或解析后文字真的变了的行才重新注册，因为无谓的重注册会重挂用户可能正在交互的行。

这一行是外壳的单个 `<button>`，所以组头 glyph 在它的祖先按钮上装**捕获阶段**的 `click`/`keydown` 监听：捕获先于根部的 React 委托处理器，因此一次 `stopPropagation()` 就能让外壳自己的 `selectPanel` 永不执行，而 `preventDefault()` 取消该行的默认激活。菜单本体是挂在 `document.body` 的覆盖层，位置由该行的 `getBoundingClientRect()` 算出，因此能溢出侧边栏的裁剪；它在显示前先量一次尺寸，`Esc` 或外部点击即关闭。
dsh-panellist README · 7.4 分组行与分组菜单：组头高亮取布局服务公开的读取面（`ctx.layout.panelInfo`），而不是外壳的 `aria-current`：外壳只在「这一行本身就是激活页」时高亮，而分组行永远不是，所以这里由成员关系驱动高亮。

dsh-panellist README · 7.5 设置导航的标记：`settings.section` 契约没有图标字段，外壳按 section id 从一份封闭清单里挑导航图标，所以这一行按**可见文本**定位：`document.body` 上的 `MutationObserver` 把 `[role="dialog"] nav button` 的文本与本插件自己的本地化标签比对，命中则打上 `data-dsh-panellist-settings-nav`，样式表据此隐藏外壳自带的 `<svg>` 并在前面画出我们的蒙版图形。全部工作在 dispose 时撤销；若始终匹配不到，就保留原生齿轮并通过自检报告——绝不报错。

dsh-panellist README · 8. 首版范围与非目标：**首版包含**：序列编辑（拖拽 + 键盘兜底）、分组、显示/隐藏（含分组内成员）、名称与图标覆盖（原图标 / 内置图标集 / 粘贴 SVG）、配置导入导出、孤儿保留与清理、中英双语界面、自检与只读降级，以及这套双语 README。

**非目标**：管理右栏卡片页签；管理「设置」对话框自身的页签顺序；改动任何插件页面的内容；替代 DSH 自带的面板列表。

```bash
section: 不启动应用也能做的静态校验

text:
dsh-panellist README · 造一个临时 profile（从内置 web 模板派生），叠加本仓库的挂载层，只打印组合树：dsh panellist-dryrun --from-default-profile web \
  --patch E:/ai-code-space/dsh-panellist/cordis.patch.yml --dump-config
```

组合树里应当出现下面这两行（已实测）：

```
section: 造一个临时 profile（从内置 web 模板派生），叠加本仓库的挂载层，只打印组合树

text:
dsh-panellist README · == E:/ai-code-space/dsh-panellist/cordis.patch.yml：- id: panellist
  name: dsh-panellist
```

这条命令不启动任何服务、不装依赖；验证完把 `$DSH_HOME/profiles/panellist-dryrun` 删掉即可。`tests/manifest.spec.ts` 把这几个一致性断言（包名 = 插件 `name` 导出 = patch 里的 `name`、运行时读取的文件都在 `files` 里、schema 版本与路由前缀单一来源）变成了每次 `pnpm check` 都会跑的用例。
